checks_run: Inspected all 61 submitted files, including learner-facing material, sealed reference code, tests, validation claims, manifest, and provenance.
Verified the immutable candidate tree before and after review and cross-checked manifest/provenance identifiers and hashes.
Built the starter and sealed reference with pinned GCC 15.2.0 under strict C17 warnings in a writable byte-identical scratch copy.
Ran the starter lexer milestone, public suite, direct VM tests, private suite, tower, environment check, and pack verifier with bounded commands.
Rebuilt the reference and VM tests with AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer and reran the submitted suites.

Ran 23 independent deterministic boundary checks covering arithmetic, short-circuiting, identifiers, locals, stack, heap, arguments, code size, source size, output-before-fault, and instruction budgets.
Probed valid deeply nested syntax with normal and sanitizer builds.
Checked diagnostic prefixes, zero-budget CLI behavior, cross-directory binary reproducibility, archive entry types, credential patterns, and sealed-material placement.
evidence: Pinned tools reported GCC 15.2.0, Python 3.11.5, GNU Binutils 2.43, and GNU Make 4.2.1.
Strict normal builds passed; the starter lexer run had 2 passes and 7 documented skips; the reference had 9/9 public, 10/10 direct VM, and 11/11 private checks pass; tower output was exactly 4242.
The submitted public, direct VM, and private suites also passed under ASan/UBSan with the pinned runtime libraries preloaded and no sanitizer diagnostic.
An independent 23-case boundary harness passed, including every checked arithmetic operation and the documented source, bytecode, local, operand-stack, and heap limits.
A valid 16,021-byte program with 8,000 nested parentheses aborted with rc=-11 normally; the sanitizer build aborted with rc=-6 and reported AddressSanitizer: stack-overflow.
A runtime overflow emitted 'runtime error: signed arithmetic overflow (line 3, column 19)' instead of the required path:line:column prefix; a compile error did use that prefix.
The CLI rejected --max-steps 0 with rc=2 even though REQUIREMENTS.md does not state a positive-only restriction and the adversarial exercise explicitly includes a zero budget.
Two clean builds from different directories produced different reference-binary SHA-256 values because -g embedded each absolute build directory.

PROVENANCE.json SHA-256 was 3dc7fc913794fd6c9205f6d0588d0a9c4370fb639ae6991b97b4f28aaff9d57a; manifest/source/project cross-links matched; all 61 files and all directories were regular entry types, and the independent credential scan had zero hits.
The manifest honestly remains GENERATED/PARTIAL with independent validation REQUIRED and makes no fuzzing, benchmarking, transfer, review, or production label claim.
limitations: Network access and the immutable catalog baseline were unavailable, so the upstream commit, external license evidence, material-baseline hash, and independent-authorship claim could not be independently verified.
Validation covered one x86_64 environment with pinned GCC; no cross-compiler, cross-architecture, or transfer validation was performed.
No coverage-guided fuzzing or benchmark was performed; the candidate also explicitly disclaims those labels.
Sanitizer reruns matched the submitted detect_leaks=0 setting, so leak detection remains unchecked; versioned runtimes also had to be preloaded because the pinned loader-name symlink was absent.

The reviewer workspace intentionally exposes sealed material. CANDIDATE contains no independently testable learner-view projection, so safe exclusion of sealed references and tests remains an external orchestrator release gate.
The read-only review copy required a byte-identical writable scratch copy for builds; only scratch permissions and build outputs were changed, never CANDIDATE.
